title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When defensive certainty becomes crowded, you end up paying a growth multiple for staple-like growth.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk Maxim

web_blocks.text: 7.1 Deconstructing Today's Price ($90.46): Retail Multiple Expansion Meets Rate Pressure

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 session close of $90.46 (with November 23 TradingView at $90.41 and Finviz at $90.57), XLP trades at 21.20x FY1 forward earnings and 25.82x trailing earnings [1, 20]. Its 30-day SEC yield is 2.34% and its trailing 12-month distribution yield is 2.43% ($2.20 per share), backed by a 0.08% gross expense ratio across $15.00 billion ($14,996.34 million) in AUM [1, 20]. Over the past 12 months, XLP gained +16.87% (+16.59% YTD), outperforming broad equities during a year marked by late-cycle AI spending scrutiny and a U.S. market Downtrend.

That defensive rally has compressed XLP's margin of safety. Two forces explain the 21.20x blended forward multiple. First, mega-cap retail winners Walmart (11.47%) and Costco (9.83%) now represent 21.30% of the fund and trade around 40x to 45x earnings [28, 29]. Second, macro risk aversion pushed capital into staples even as the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield climbed to 5.04% (and the 2-year yield to 4.76%) on November 19, 2026. At 2.43%, XLP's cash yield sits 261 basis points below the 10-year risk-free rate, leaving zero room for multiple expansion.

web_blocks.text: 7.2 Reverse DCF: What Today's $90.46 Price Already Assumes

web_blocks.html: We invert the valuation math to test what today's $90.46 price embeds. Against an 8.0% institutional equity hurdle rate—appropriate when 10-year Treasuries yield 5.04%—XLP's 2.43% distribution yield requires 5.57% annual price appreciation just to clear the hurdle. If the forward P/E holds flat at 21.20x, constituents must deliver 5.6% to 8.0% annual EPS growth.

Our refreshed Pass 1 audit shows mixed underlying growth. Walmart raised FY27 constant-currency sales guidance to +4.9%–5.2% and adjusted operating income to +8.0%–8.6% [31]. Costco delivered $303.15 billion in FY26 revenue and $9.38 billion in free cash flow [33], while Coca-Cola unit case volume rebounded +5% in Q3 2026 [35] and P&G organic sales rose +4.0% [34]. However, three drags cap look-through EPS growth near 6.5%: (1) one-time 2026 IEEPA tariff refunds ($1.3B YTD at Target, $184M at Costco) [32, 33] will not repeat in 2027; (2) P&G expanded its restructuring to ~$2.0 billion [34]; and (3) U.S. private-label unit share sits at 23.5% [14]. Applying 6.5% annualized EPS growth over 15 months (from $4.27 implied FY1 EPS to $4.63) and modest multiple mean reversion to 20.6x produces a $95.50 base-case fair value (+5.57% price upside, +8.00% total return).

web_blocks.the_number: $95.50 base-case 15-month fair value (+5.57% price upside from $90.46; +8.00% total return with 2.43% yield)
web_blocks.how_calculated: Starts from $90.46 CMP at 21.20x FY1 EPS ($4.27 implied look-through EPS). Applies 6.5% annualized look-through EPS growth over 1.25 years ($4.63 forward EPS) and modest compression to 20.6x P/E, yielding $95.50.
web_blocks.the_inputs: CMP $90.46; FY1 P/E 21.20x; WMT+COST 21.30% at 40x–45x P/E; FactSet 8.75% EPS growth haircut to 6.5% for IEEPA refund normalization and CPG restructuring; US10Y 5.04%; 2.43% distribution yield.
web_blocks.the_range: $78.50 Bear Case (18.0x compressed multiple on ~4.5% EPS growth) to $103.50 Bull Case (22.2x defensive-bid multiple on 8.75% consensus EPS growth).
web_blocks.if_off: If retail margins compress after IEEPA tariff refunds roll off or 10Y yields push above 5.25%, fair value drops toward $78.50–$82.00.

web_blocks.html: Multiple-Normalization Stress Test (18.5x Historical Norm): Our $95.50 base case assumes XLP holds a 20.6x forward P/E—above its 18.5x–20.0x historical staples norm—despite 5.04% 10-year Treasury yields and 21.30% concentration in Walmart and Costco at 40x–45x earnings. If XLP merely mean-reverts to 18.5x on $4.63 forward EPS, base fair value falls to $85.66 (-5.31% price / -2.88% total return) and probability-weighted EV drops to $88.33, sitting below the $88.51 support shelf. Under a combined stress of 3.0% annualized EPS growth ($4.43 forward EPS) as 2026 IEEPA tariff refunds lap, fair value compresses to $81.96 at 18.5x and $79.74 at 18.0x.

web_blocks.mechanism: Yield-starved investors rotated heavily into U.S. consumer staples in 2015–2016, pushing XLP above 21.5x forward earnings. When Treasury yields rose and private-label competition slowed CPG organic growth in 2017–2018, the sector endured a multi-quarter valuation de-rating.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: XLP stalled near $55–$58 for nearly two years and fell -17.3% peak-to-trough in early 2018 (from $58.65 to $48.52) despite steady dividends.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Even durable defensive cash flows suffer multi-quarter dead money or 15%+ drawdowns when bought above 21x forward earnings against rising Treasury yields.

book_paragraphs: Now that you and I have completed our refreshed price-blind audit of XLP's 34 constituents, its 0.08% fee structure, and the new Q3 2026 filings—including one-time IEEPA tariff refunds at Target and Costco—we open the market screen. At the November 20, 2026 close of $90.46, XLP trades at 21.20x FY1 forward earnings and 25.82x trailing earnings, with a 2.43% distribution yield across $15.00 billion in AUM.

Two forces explain why a slow-growing staples basket trades above 21x forward earnings. First, Walmart at 11.47% and Costco at 9.83% together make up 21.30% of the fund, and both retail giants trade around 40x to 45x earnings. Second, investors rotated into defensive staples during 2026's broader equity Downtrend. Yet on November 19, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield reached 5.04%, putting XLP's 2.43% cash yield 261 basis points below risk-free Treasuries.

Let's invert the valuation math to see what $90.46 already assumes. Against an 8.0% institutional hurdle rate, XLP needs 5.57% annual price appreciation on top of its 2.43% yield. While Walmart raised FY27 guidance and Coca-Cola unit case volume rebounded +5% in Q3, one-time IEEPA tariff refunds will lap in 2027, P&G expanded its restructuring to $2.0 billion, and private-label share sits at 23.5%. Haircutting look-through EPS growth to 6.5% over 15 months and applying a 20.6x multiple yields a $95.50 base-case fair value—just +5.57% above $90.46.

Stress-testing that 20.6x base multiple reveals why valuation discipline must override defensive comfort. If XLP merely mean-reverts to 18.5x—the low end of its 18.5x to 20.0x historical norm—on $4.63 forward EPS, base fair value drops to $85.66 and probability-weighted expected value falls to $88.33, already below the $88.51 support shelf. If one-time 2026 IEEPA tariff refunds also slow look-through EPS growth to 3.0% ($4.43 forward EPS), fair value compresses to $81.96 at 18.5x and $79.74 at 18.0x.

History warns against paying peak multiples for defensive safety. In 2016, yield-seeking investors bid XLP above 21.5x forward earnings, only to endure two years of flat returns and a -17.3% drawdown in early 2018 when rates rose. Compared with peers VDC, FSTA, IYK, and RSPS, XLP is still the premier institutional vehicle at 0.08% with $15.00 billion in AUM. Even the best vehicle requires entry-price discipline.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Paying Growth Multiples for Safety
book_callouts.text: When 10-year Treasuries yield 5.04% and XLP yields 2.43%, you cannot rely on multiple expansion. Buying at $90.46 leaves just +5.57% upside to our $95.50 base target, making entry discipline near support essential.
